decisions.rationale: DurableExecutor creates one CommitRecord, appends it once, then immediately awaits `_commitJournal.CommitAsync(ct)` before applying state/publishing; no batching or accumulation appears in that commit path.

IdempotentSink defaults to `DurabilityMode.FsyncAlways`; `WriteAsync` appends then awaits `_wal.CommitAsync`. DurableExecutor publishes each outbox item via `sink.WriteAsync`, adding a second durable commit for local delivery.

No group commit is implemented inside DurableExecution, but the repo already has a group-commit WAL mechanism: `FileWriteAheadLog` documents `Group commit = many appends, one fsync` and `DurabilityMode.FsyncEveryNms` exists.
Seal directory lists exactly the six cited files, and repo-scope `rg SealSet` returned no matches, so no symbol named `SealSet` exists at this pin.

decisions.rationale: Docs say the seed is in memory only, fresh per launch/session, never persisted; `InMemoryDeviceSealKey` constructor calls `RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes` and derives the public key from that seed.

Ed25519AmuletVerifier fixed-time compares the seal public key to one trusted key and returns `untrusted key` on mismatch; the Seal dir's only trust-anchor class is DeviceSealTrustAnchor exposing the local key.
Seal docs are single-root, but repo-scope search finds the missing multi-key anchor elsewhere: `PeerSetTrustAnchor` is an ordered multi-key Ed25519 trust root with `PeerSetAmuletVerifier`.
EnforceCaveats switches only exp/scope/audience/resource/tbl/kpfx and the default returns `unknown caveat key`, so new hop-chain caveat keys require editing this verifier.

SigningPayload writes only `block` and `macaroon`; FetchDescriptor has ResourceId/Audience/Scope/IssuedForIdentity, and Macaroon has Identifier/Caveats/Sig. No signed hop, predecessor, sequence, or cycle field appears there.

Macaroon docs define an HMAC chain over identifier plus ordered caveats, and Chain applies HMAC over id then each caveat. IDeviceSealKey says the HMAC key is mint-time only and never leaves the signer.

`exp` is parsed as `DateOnly` and enforced with `now > exp`; the minter accepts a DateOnly exp. The 122 ms RTT evidence supports the stated 33.9 h arithmetic, so an exp=today run would fail after the date advances.

DurableExecutor retains `_committed` and `_byTriggerId`; IdempotentSink retains `_seen` and `_records`. Replay/open and write paths only add; grep found no eviction/compaction/removal in DurableExecution.

DurableExecutor.OpenAsync replays `commitJournal.ReplayAsync(0, ct)` and folds each record; IdempotentSink.OpenAsync replays `wal.ReplayAsync(0)` and rebuilds seen/records, so recovery scans total retained history.

The cited slice has no CRC/checksum/resume hits, but repo-scope search disproves the absence: Mailbox FileWriteAheadLog frames include crc32 and replay truncates torn records; IWriteAheadLog documents resume after crash.

The out-of-slice definitions are in repo: DurabilityMode says FsyncAlways fsyncs on every commit, and FileWriteAheadLog.CommitAsync calls `_active.Flush(flushToDisk: _mode != OsFlushOnly)`. Cost is unmeasured, but real fsync semantics are verifiable.

README says fixtures are hand-authored JSONL replayed by dry-run with no device I/O; PASS fixtures carry `sessionId`/`commit` dry-run and synthetic `atMs`; ledger GREEN is the controller dry-run path.

Seal code is in namespace Olamnit.Shared.Yngenios.Seal; DurableExecutor is Olamnit.Kernel.DurableExecution and imports Kernel namespaces. Kernel.csproj has no ProjectReference to Olamnit.Shared, so using Seal in Kernel would require adding one.
Ed25519Signer copies `message` with `message.ToArray()` in both Sign and Verify, so each sign/verify call allocates a managed message copy.
